newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-DONALD GIVES SOUTH AFRICA TEST SUPREMACY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DONALD GIVES SOUTH AFRICA TEST SUPREMACY.

text.p: Some superb fast bowling from Allan Donald gave South Africa a stranglehold on the first test against India on Friday.
Donald, spearhead of a four-man pace attack, took five for 40 as India were routed for 100 in only 39.1 overs -- their lowest five-day total against South Africa.

That gave South Africa an imposing first innings lead of 135 and opener Andrew Hudson, who made the top score of 80 first time around, and Adam Bacher then built on that with a second wicket partnership of 111 as the home side closed on 164 for four in their second innings.
Hudson (52) batted authoritatively for his second 50 of the match and Bacher, on his test debut, made a composed 55 for South Africa to establish a commanding lead of 299 going into the third day.
South African coach Bob Woolmer later said, however, that the lead was still far from sufficient.
"I want our batters to get as many runs as possible - you don't really feel comfortable until you get a lead of around 400," he said.

While India had the better of the first day in dismissing South Africa for 235, their batsmen struggled on day two against a fast bowling quartet who took full advantage of a pitch offering both pace and bounce.

Donald bowled with accuracy and hostility for his seventh five-wicket haul at test level. He was well supported by Shaun Pollock and all-rounder Brian McMillan, who took two wickets each. Lance Klusener picked up the other.
No Indian batsman reached 20 as they were dismissed for the third lowest test total ever compiled at Kingsmead after Australia's 75 and South Africa's 99 in the same match during the 1949-50 series.
Saurav Ganguly had the highest score of 16 but the key wicket was that of Indian captain Sachin Tendulkar.
From successive deliveries he dispatched Donald to the boundary but next ball he was comprehensively beaten by a rapid off-cutter to be bowled through the gate for 15.
It was a delivery that surprised even Donald, who has now taken 129 wickets in his 28 tests.
"It's the best test wicket I've taken," he said. "I didn't realise that it had cut back so much until I saw the television replay much later."
There was a hint of controversy over the dismissal of David Johnson who was given out, caught by Bacher at short-leg, after being hit on the shoulder by a Donald bumper.

Johnson was clearly unhappy about the dismissal and was later severely reprimanded by International Cricket Council (ICC) match referee Barry Jarman for showing dissent towards New Zealand umpire Steve Dunne who gave him out.

Although South Africa again lost the early wicket of left-handed opener Gary Kirsten, Hudson and Bacher pressed home the advantage with their partnership of 111 -- the largest stand of the match so far.
Bacher reached his maiden test 50 from 93 balls with a cut for four off the wrist-spin of Anil Kumble but he departed five runs later, flicking the same bowler to Tendulkar at short mid-wicket.

Daryll Cullinan also failed for the second time in the game, caught behind off the persevering Prasad for three, but captain Hansie Cronje (17 not out) and Herschelle Gibbs (25 not out) added 44 together before the close.
